messages:
Alex M.: FYI — last night 23:42 UTC we saw a P95 latency spike on /v1/generate (user-facing). Postmortem in progress but we need a short-lived SLO plan + tracked remediation owners/timelines. Starting thread to capture owners and dashboard/alert changes.

Rina S.: Can you paste current error budget burn and the dashboard link? also which SLOs are impacted (P95 vs P99 vs throughput)? :eyes:

Sam (oncall): Current error burn: ~18% over last 24h, mostly from 23:40–23:55. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/s/requests/latency (private link). P95 up ~2.3x, P99 unchanged-ish.

Jiayi L.: I looked at traces — big tail caused by batching delays when autoscaler was scaling down. Long cold-starts + large micro-batches for some requests. Will own batching config remediation + canary. ETA: EOD Wed (72h). I'll open a ticket.

Marc P.: I'll own the SLO dashboard and runbook updates. Plan to add a temporary panel showing per-model batch size and last_seen_node_age. ETA: Fri COB.

Alex M.: Proposal: temporary P95 SLO relaxation from 200ms -> 250ms for 72h to avoid alert thrash while we roll fix. Keep P99 and throughput SLOs unchanged. Also adjust paging alert to avoid cascading on call. Thoughts?

Rina S.: I can approve a 72h relaxation but not longer. Need an explicit rollback time and owner assigned. Also update the error-budget policy doc.

Sam (oncall): I'll handle alert threshold changes and put a follow-up monitor in place. Making a small alert PR now: change alert P95 firing threshold to 260ms and add a suppress window for flapping during the 72h window.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-034 created: latency spike on /v1/generate. Severity: Sev3. Pager muted per oncall instructions. (automated)

Jiayi L.: Created remediation ticket INF-1234: "Reduce batch window + ensure grace autoscale" with steps and rollback. Link: https://tickets.redwood/internal/INF-1234. Assigned to Jiayi L. ETA Wed EOD.

Marc P.: Dashboard PR opened: https://git.redwood/dashboards/pulls/412. Updated legend and added the per-model batch size chart. Requesting review from @Rina S.

Rina S.: Reviewing dashboard PR. Also adding a short section to runbook about recurring tail-latency pattern we keep seeing on scale-down cycles. This looks like a recurring incident pattern we need to track across the quarter.

Alex M.: To summarize and assign owners: Jiayi -> batching fix (INF-1234) ETA Wed. Sam -> alert changes + monitor (PR/commit) in next 2h. Marc -> dashboard + runbook update ETA Fri. Rina -> SLO relaxation approve + rollback policy doc. I'll own cross-team sync and follow-up in next all-hands.

Sam (oncall): Alert PR merged. I'll keep eyes on the error budget and post back in 12h with burn delta.

Jiayi L.: Canary deploy started (3 nodes). Canary config snippet:
```
canary_instances: 3
batch_timeout_ms: 10
prewarm=true
```
Will report perf after 30m.

Marc P.: Noted recurring pattern: scale-down + cold-starts -> temporary micro-batches -> tail latency. Adding to quarterly recurring-incident spreadsheet so platform team can prioritize a more durable fix (node prewarm + smarter autoscale).

Rina S.: After canary, if stable, we'll rollback the P95 relaxation earlier. Keep the change window to 72h maximum. Also add an alert: "batch_size_spike" to detect future regressions faster.

IncidentBot: Update: INF-1234 status -> in_progress (Jiayi L.).

Alex M.: Checking back in — Jiayi, how did canary run?

Jiayi L.: Canary looked good. P95 reduced to ~190ms on canary nodes, no errors. Rolling to 20% traffic now. Will continue to monitor and post final notes.

Sam (oncall): Error budget burn rate dropped to 4% over the last 4h after canary started. Will keep monitoring.

Marc P.: Merged dashboard + runbook changes. PRs: dashboards#412 merged, runbook#99 merged. Added link to incident notes.

Rina S.: Closing notes: Temporary SLO change applied at 00:10 UTC, scheduled rollback at +72h unless remediation completes earlier. Owners and tickets logged. Recommend weekly check-ins for recurring-incident spreadsheet until root cause fully mitigated. :thumbsup:

Alex M.: Thanks all — leaving this thread open for final confirmation. If no regressions and INF-1234 lands, we'll close the postmortem loop and mark action items resolved.

Sam (oncall): No regressions in last 12h. Will report again at 24h and then we can close loop if stable.

Jiayi L.: INF-1234 marked resolved after full rollout. Linking final perf test: https://perf.redwood/results/inf-1234-final.

Alex M.: Excellent. Closing loop: SLOs restored to original thresholds at 1976543875 (rollback), error budget burn normalized. Thanks team.

(End of thread)
